title: SGLang and RadixAttention for Prefix-Heavy Workloads

questions.question: What token count does token_count assign to the SYSTEM segment?
questions.explanation: The local token_count function returns 2000 for SYSTEM, 500 for DOC_ segments, 300 for TOOLS, and 60 for Q_ segments.

questions.question: What does RadixCache.walk return for a request whose first two segment paths are already present?
options: The number of evicted leaves
The tokens reused along the longest matching prefix
The request's branch count only
The total KV budget in blocks
questions.explanation: walk follows the path until the first missing node, sums token_count for matched segments, and updates their last_used timestamps.

questions.question: How does CACHE_AWARE rank a Request before dispatch?
options: By request ID in ascending order
By the shortest prompt first
By the maximum branch_count times cumulative prefix-token sum
By randomizing all leaves equally
questions.explanation: The score examines every prefix and takes max(branch_count[prefix] * cumulative token count), then sorts requests descending.

questions.question: Why does workload_scrambled generally have poor radix reuse?
options: It removes the SYSTEM segment entirely
It uses a larger cache budget than workload_rag
It gives every request the same question ID
It shuffles SYSTEM, TOOLS, and DOC so shared prefixes no longer align
questions.explanation: Radix reuse requires identical leading paths; scrambling the prefix segments makes otherwise shared content appear at different tree positions.

questions.question: What resource limit makes eviction visible in the toy RadixCache?
options: 160 blocks of 16 tokens
16 blocks of 160 tokens
80 requests with no block accounting
2,000 blocks for SYSTEM only
questions.explanation: KV_BUDGET_BLOCKS is 160 and BLOCK_TOKENS is 16; insert evicts least-recently-used leaves when this block budget would be exceeded.

questions.question: What design change does the lesson associate with a rise from roughly 7% to 74% cache hits?
options: Increasing every question to 2,000 tokens
Moving dynamic content out of the stable prompt prefix
Disabling the radix tree and using FCFS
Reducing the cache budget to one block
questions.explanation: Keeping stable SYSTEM/TOOLS content at the front and moving dynamic material later creates reusable leading paths for RadixAttention.
